canvas-01-1.description: A strip along Kingwood Avenue on the south-east edge of Frenchtown, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that the avenue runs straight up the sheet; north points to the upper right. It is the left-hand third of Sheet 1, which also carries the town's key map, index and a second map part. The strip begins at the top with the iron bridge carrying Kingwood Avenue over the Big Nishisakaway Creek, where the Creek or Hollow Road branches off to the east along the creek, and runs south-east past Private Drive, Eros (marked as an arbitrary name) and a short unnamed street to the fork where the Public Road leaves the avenue, ending in open land at the bottom of the sheet. Most of the frontage is detached frame dwellings with stables and sheds, set on large lots, many of them partly blank. Industry is represented by the Frenchtown Silk Co. weaving mill (concrete block) near the creek, a livery, a slaughter house and storage sheds along the Creek or Hollow Road, and Cooley's Chicken Hatchery on the east side of the avenue below Eros. Water pipes are drawn along the avenue and the creek road, with hydrants and a fire alarm box, and street widths are marked (35 to 55 feet on the avenue, 40 feet on the Public Road). Block numbers 9, 50 and 110 are printed in the open land on either side. The area west of the avenue towards the top is only sketched with lot lines.
notes: Turned on the page: Kingwood Avenue runs up the sheet, north is about 59 degrees clockwise from straight up.
Creek or Hollow Road is Creek Road today.
Eros (printed as arbitrary) is Ward Street today; the street marked Not Named is East Washington Avenue; the Public Road is Ridge Road (identified from their spacing along Kingwood Avenue).
Drawn about 1 percent off the 100 ft scale; placed from four junctions all on Kingwood Avenue, so the rotation rests on the line of the avenue.

Sheet 1. Title, key map (800 ft to an inch, not georeferenced), index and water/fire notes in the upper right; two map parts at 100 ft to an inch: part 1 Kingwood Avenue strip (left third, turned on the page, north about 59 degrees clockwise), part 2 Harrison Street / Milford Road from 9th to 12th Streets (lower right, north up). Fainter ink than sheets 2 to 5.

canvas-01-2.description: The north end of Frenchtown between the Pennsylvania Railroad's Belvidere Division and Milford Road, from the borough limits just north of 12th Street south to 9th Street, drawn at 100 feet to an inch in the lower right quarter of Sheet 1 (the upper right holds the key map and index). North is up. Harrison Street runs down the sheet with 12th, 11th and 10th Streets crossing it to Milford Road on the east, beyond which a steep hillside is noted; 10th Street west of Harrison is marked not opened, and 9th Street is just reached at the bottom edge. Most of the part is open ground: the large block 104 west of Harrison is an athletic field with a grandstand, and block 103 between 11th and 12th Streets is empty. Built-up land is limited to a row of frame dwellings along the south side of the borough limits above 12th Street (blocks 101 and 102), a few dwellings with stables on Harrison Street between 10th and 11th Streets (block 105), and dwellings around 10th Street, one of them a tile house. At the bottom, next to the railroad, is a concrete-floored warehouse. The railroad line is drawn along the left edge of the part. Water pipes, a hose house and fire alarm boxes are marked on Harrison Street, and the street widths are given as 50 feet for Harrison and the numbered streets and 50 feet for Milford Road.
notes: P.R.R. (Belvidere Div.) along the west side; the line is abandoned today.
9th Street is not in the OpenStreetMap extract; 12th, 11th and 10th Streets, Harrison Street and Milford Road keep their names.
Borough limits drawn along the north side of 12th Street's blocks.

Sheet 1. Title, key map (800 ft to an inch, not georeferenced), index and water/fire notes in the upper right; two map parts at 100 ft to an inch: part 1 Kingwood Avenue strip (left third, turned on the page, north about 59 degrees clockwise), part 2 Harrison Street / Milford Road from 9th to 12th Streets (lower right, north up). Fainter ink than sheets 2 to 5.

sheet-2-1.description: The business centre of Frenchtown, on the Delaware River, from 3rd Street south to the short street at the foot of the sheet (Lott Street today), between Front Street and the Pennsylvania Railroad on the west and the Big Nishisakaway Creek on the east. North is up. Bridge Street crosses the middle of the sheet from the railroad depot towards the river bridge; Harrison Street, South Harrison Street, Trenton Avenue (also named Cemetery) and Race Street meet it, and Race Street with Kingwood Avenue runs north-east to the iron bridge over the creek. The blocks along Bridge Street are drawn densely with brick stores, lodge rooms, a bank, the post office, a moving picture hall and the National Hotel at Race Street. Institutions include the M.E. Church (also used as a temporary public school), the Baptist Church, a stone public school with the town hall and fire department, and a garage. Industry lines the railroad and the creek: C. White's planing mill and Jacob White's lumber and coal yard at 3rd Street, I.L. Niece Lumber Co. west of the tracks, the passenger and freight depot, R.W. Kerr Chicken Hatchery No. 1, and Worman and Lear's flour mill on the tail race with the head race beside it. A separate inset at the lower right, outlined by a heavy line, shows R.W. Kerr's chicken hatchery and ice houses 1 7/8 miles north of the post office; it is not part of this map part. Street widths, house numbers and water pipes are given throughout.
notes: Front (Railroad Av.) is Front Street today south of Bridge Street; north of it the street is Railroad Avenue.
Trenton Av. (Cemetery): Cemetery is the alternative name given in the index; Trenton Avenue today.
Race is Race Street today; the unnamed 20 ft street at the foot of the sheet is Lott Street.
Inset (part 2, R.W. Kerr chicken hatchery and ice houses, 1 7/8 miles north of the post office) not georeferenced: no street junction on it.
P.R.R. (Belvidere Div.) and the depot along the west side; the line is now the Delaware and Raritan Canal Trail.

Sheet 2, 50 ft. Business centre: 3rd St to Lott St (unnamed 20 ft street at the foot), Front St (Railroad Av.) to Race St and the Big Nishisakaway Creek; Bridge, Harrison, S. Harrison, Trenton Av. (Cemetery), Kingwood Av. Part 1 main map; part 2 is an inset of R.W. Kerr's chicken hatchery and ice houses 1 7/8 miles north of the post office (no street junction, not placed).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: R.W. Kerr chicken hatchery and ice houses, located 1 7/8 miles north of the post office (no street junction (only a railroad siding and a road), and outside the reference box; needs a modern feature identifiable on the inset (the former railroad siding), or a parcel corner once the site is located).

sheet-3.description: The north side of Frenchtown between the Pennsylvania Railroad and Milford Road, from 9th Street south to 6th Street, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north up. Harrison Street runs down the middle of the sheet, crossed by 8th, 7th and 6th Streets; Railroad Avenue appears at the lower left, and a steep hillside is noted east of Milford Road (also labelled avenue). The north-west block is taken up by the Frenchtown Porcelain Co. works, which made porcelain spark plugs: kilns, turning and flat reaming, tapping and boring, glazing, a machine shop, power house, clay storage and shipping rooms, with notes on its watchman, power, heating and hose. South of it, west of Harrison Street, are dwellings and, at 7th Street, a warehouse, a wagon shed and lumber shed, with the Crosby Mfg. Co. doll carriage factory (brick, with its own steam engine) in the block below. East of Harrison the blocks are lined with frame dwellings, and between 7th and 6th Streets stands W.A. Hillpots' chicken hatchery with a concrete-block packing house, greenhouse and a seed mail order building. The block north of 8th Street east of Harrison is nearly empty, crossed only by the compass. The west margin notes the railroad and the Delaware River beyond. Water pipes, hydrants, fire alarm boxes and street widths (50 feet for Harrison Street and Milford Road, 50 feet for the numbered streets) are marked.
notes: Milford R'd (Av.) is Milford Road today; Railroad Av. is Railroad Avenue.
9th Street is not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
Penna R.R. (Belvidere Division) along the west edge, now the Delaware and Raritan Canal Trail.
Sheet 3, 50 ft. 9th to 6th Streets between the railroad (Railroad Av.) and Milford Rd (Av.); Harrison St down the middle. Frenchtown Porcelain Co., Crosby Mfg Co., W.A. Hillpots hatchery. One part.

sheet-4.description: The middle of Frenchtown's residential grid, from 6th Street south to 3rd Street between Railroad Avenue, which follows the Pennsylvania Railroad and the Delaware River on the west, and Milford Road on the east, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north up. Harrison Street runs down the centre, crossed by 6th, 5th, 4th and 3rd Streets, and the blocks are divided into regular narrow lots. Nearly every lot carries a frame dwelling, most of two storeys with porches and rear stables or auto houses; a few are brick or stone (a row of stone dwellings on the north side of 4th Street east of Harrison). Institutions are the Presbyterian Church with its chapel and an auto and horse shed on the south side of 4th Street, and the library on the east side of Harrison Street near 3rd Street. Small industries are a chair factory with woodworking shop on 6th Street west of Harrison, a slaughter house storage building in the block north-east of Harrison and 5th Street, and lumber sheds along Railroad Avenue. The block numbers 20, 21 and 22 and the alley lines through the middle of each block are printed. The west margin notes the railroad and the Delaware River beyond, and a steep hillside is noted east of Milford Road. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 8 inches, hydrants, fire alarm boxes and street widths (33 to 50 feet) are marked along the streets.
notes: Street names unchanged today (Harrison Street, Milford Road, Railroad Avenue, 3rd to 6th Streets).
P.R.R. & Delaware River beyond noted in the west margin; the railroad is now the Delaware and Raritan Canal Trail.
Sheet 4, 50 ft. 6th to 3rd Streets between Railroad Av. and Milford Rd; Harrison St down the middle. Pilot sheet (12 of 12 junctions detected). One part.

sheet-5-1.description: The south end of Frenchtown between the Pennsylvania Railroad's Belvidere Division and the Big Nishisakaway Creek, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north up, in the left part of Sheet 5; a heavy line separates it from the part to the east of the creek. Front Street (also named Railroad Avenue) runs down the west side beside the tracks and Trenton Avenue (also named Cemetery) down the east side, joined by a short unnamed 20 ft street at the top (Lott Street today), by a narrow lane and by Railroad Street. The blocks between them hold frame dwellings on narrow lots facing Front Street and Trenton Avenue, the Municipal Light Co. plant (a dynamo with a 100 horsepower engine, not in operation) and a carpenter's shop. South of Railroad Street the Big Nishisakaway Creek and, lower down, the Little Nishisakaway Creek cross the sheet towards the Delaware, with Trenton Avenue carried over them on an iron bridge and a stone bridge. The land between and below the creeks is mostly open: W.J. Weiss Monumental Works, the old and vacant buildings formerly of the Standard Flint and Spar Co., and Habisons Dairies' creamery beside the railroad are the only works, with a few scattered dwellings along the road south. The west margin notes the Delaware River beyond the railroad. Water pipes, hydrants, a fire alarm box and street widths are marked.
notes: Railroad St. is Hawk Street today; the narrow lane north of it is Kerr Street; the unnamed 20 ft street at the top is Lott Street.
Front (Railroad Av.) south of Lott Street is Railroad Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Placed from hand-picked junctions (the detector found none at first); Hawk Street's junctions agree with Lott Street's to 2 to 3 m.

Sheet 5, 50 ft, two parts divided by a heavy line along the creek: part 1 (west, north up) Front St (Railroad Av.) and Trenton Av. south of Lott St, Railroad St (= Hawk Street), Big and Little Nishisakaway Creeks; part 2 (east, turned, north about 20 degrees anticlockwise) Milford Rd, Everittstown Rd (= Everittstown Hill Road), Cedar St, Race St, water company pumping station.

sheet-5-2.description: The east side of Frenchtown beyond the Big Nishisakaway Creek, along Milford Road and Everittstown Road, drawn at 50 feet to an inch in the right part of Sheet 5 and turned so that north points to the upper left; a heavy line separates it from the part west of the creek. Milford Road runs diagonally down the sheet past the end of 3rd Street to meet Race Street at the bottom, and Everittstown Road runs up the sheet from that junction, with Cedar Street joining it from the north-west at a sharp angle near the top and a short unnamed street leading off Cedar Street. The ground between Milford Road and Everittstown Road (blocks 52, 108 and 109) is divided into large lots with a few frame dwellings and stables. East of Everittstown Road, on block 51, are a few more dwellings and a coop, and below them the steep bank of the Big Nishisakaway Creek, with a wooden flume and the head race, and at the bottom right the Frenchtown Water Co. pumping station with its pumps and reservoir pipe. A water pipe to the reservoir runs up Everittstown Road, and hydrants, fire alarm boxes and street widths (28 to 39 feet) are marked.
notes: Turned on the page: north is about 20 degrees anticlockwise from straight up.
Everittstown Rd is Everittstown Hill Road today; Cedar is Cedar Street.
Placed from three junctions (two detected, Cedar / Everittstown hand-picked); an exact three-point fit with no check, low confidence.
